newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's offshore banking assets rise in 4th Qtr.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's offshore banking assets rise in 4th Qtr.

text.p: Total assets of offshore banking units (OBUs) in Bahrain rose to $66.92 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996 from $64.25 billion a year-earlier period, official figures showed on Monday.
A Bahrain Monetary Agency (BMA) quarterly bulletin said the assets were down compared with $67.12 billion three months earlier.
The BMA, Bahrain's central bank, did not say how many OBU's were operating in the island at end-1996, but a BMA official told Reuters there were 46 OBUs licensed at end-1996.
There were 75 units in Bahrain at the start of the oil boom in the mid 1970s and their assets peaked at $72.58 billion at end-1989.

Assets of commercial banks rose to 2.69 billion dinars ($7.13 billion) in the fourth quarter of 1996 from 2.62 billion dinars in the same period the previous year and against 2.53 billion dinars in the third quarter of 1996.
Bahrain is the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
